title: Sena Dynasty
capsule: The Sena dynasty, of South Indian Brahmin-Kshatriya origin, rose to dominance in Bengal following the decline of the Pala Empire and by the reign of Vijayasena (c. 1095–1158) controlled most of Bengal including Varendra, Radha, and Vanga regions. Ballalasena (c. 1158–1179) codified the Hindu social order in Bengal through his work on dharmaśāstra, while Lakshmanasena (c. 1179–1206) patronized Sanskrit literature and oversaw the court of poet Jayadeva, author of the Gītagovinda. Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khilji's rapid cavalry raid on Nabadwip around 1203 destroyed the Sena seat of power, though peripheral Sena rulers held fragments of territory in eastern Bengal until the mid-thirteenth century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Sena core territory in Bengal is reasonably well attested through copper-plate grants and numismatic evidence, but the outer margins of their polity are inferred from scattered literary and epigraphic sources.
